metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: State whether /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code is a shared external named volume or a container-local path, and if shared, reuse (or explicitly justify not reusing) the tickets clone's flock-on-inode serialization + resolvable-ref poison-recovery.
evidence: Plan: 'clones the CODE side into /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code ... Like the tickets clone this is backgrounded'

The tickets store is a SHARED external named volume: docker-compose.yml:399 'gerrit_mcp_tickets:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets' and :441 'gerrit_mcp_tickets: external: true'; created from SITE_SUBDIRS (compose-up.sh:30) -- the same /var/gerrit/site/ namespace the plan's new path sits in

That shared volume is exactly why mcp-entrypoint.sh carries flock-on-the-directory-inode serialization + a resolvable-HEAD poison check (reclone_store, store_head_resolves, MCP_RECLONE_LOCK_WAIT) -- comment at lines 77-102: a second blue-green container into the same volume 'would clear the directory out from under it'

If mcp-code is likewise a shared named volume, a backgrounded clone that clears/re-clones can poison a peer container's in-progress clone with no serialization; if it is container-local, that concern evaporates but the plan should say the path is per-container and NOT an external volume
findings.finding: The fix does not specify whether the new code clone at /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code is a shared external named volume or a container-local path, which determines whether it inherits the tickets clone's shared-volume poisoning race and its flock/poison-recovery machinery.
scenarios: A blue-green deploy starts a second mcp container into a shared mcp-code volume while the first is still cloning main; a clear+re-clone poisons the peer, matching the unfit-beneficial-whimbrel-class failure the tickets machinery exists to prevent
An operator restart (restart: always, no deploy flock) races a concurrent code clone on the same shared volume
findings.suggested_fix: Make the code clone container-local (ephemeral per-container, outside the /var/gerrit/site external-volume namespace) so no cross-container serialization is needed; or, if it must be a shared named volume, add it to SITE_SUBDIRS and route its clone through the same reclone_store flock + head-resolves poison check as the tickets store.

findings.checklist_item: State whether /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code is a persistent named volume or an ephemeral per-container checkout, and if persistent enumerate the parity edit sites (compose volumes:/mount, mcp_run_new -v, and the compose-up.sh volume-creation list).
evidence: docker-compose.yml:391/399 mounts `gerrit_mcp_tickets:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets` for the tickets store
autodeploy.sh:391 mcp_run_new carries `-v gerrit_mcp_tickets:/var/gerrit/site/mcp-tickets`
test_autodeploy_mcp_run_new_mounts_the_same_ticket_store (tests/unit/test_mcp_on_box_infra.py:315) enforces the volume:path pair in mcp_run_new
docker-compose.yml:396-399 notes the tickets volume is an external named volume created by compose-up.sh's SITE_SUBDIRS list
The plan says the code clone is "Like the tickets clone" but names no volume for /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code
findings.finding: The plan adds a new clone target /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code but does not state its storage backing, so a required set of parity edit sites (a named-volume mount in compose `volumes:` AND in `mcp_run_new -v`, plus creation in the site volume list) may be unenumerated — the sibling tickets store it is modeled on uses the persistent `gerrit_mcp_tickets` named volume spelled in exactly those three places.
findings.location: Fix → Shape ("clones the CODE side into /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code")
scenarios: A container restarts or is blue-green replaced and re-clones ~200k commits every boot because /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code has no persistent volume
The docker-run (blue-green) path silently diverges from compose because only one of the two got a code-volume mount, failing the parity oracle or serving an unprovisioned root

evidence: vague/subjective terms present: better
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define idempotent create + retire behavior for /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code (skip-if-present-and-fetch, or clean-and-reclone) so re-provisioning does not error on an existing directory.
evidence: Plan: 'provision_store gains a sibling that clones the CODE side into /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code' — clone is not idempotent by default; a second clone into an existing non-empty dir errors.
No cleanup/retire path or 'skip if present / fetch instead' behavior is described for the mcp-code directory across provision runs.
findings.finding: The clone into /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code has no defined behavior for re-provisioning: if the directory already exists (container restart / re-run of provision), `git clone` into a populated path fails, and the plan specifies no idempotent create/RETIRE path.
findings.location: Fix > Shape / Ordering ('provision_store gains a sibling that clones...')
scenarios: On container restart or a re-invocation of provisioning, the clone step errors on an existing directory, leaving REBAR_ROOT pointing at a possibly partial or stale checkout.
Operator sees provisioning noise or a half-materialized clone; gates keep failing without a clear signal.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror whatever the existing tickets-clone provisioning does for re-runs (fetch if the dir already contains a valid clone, otherwise clean and clone) and note that parity explicitly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the REBAR_ROOT / mcp-code provisioning contract and the compose<->mcp_run_new parity requirement in a doc/ADR or AGENTS.md so the constraint outlives the ticket.
evidence: 'REBAR_ROOT is set to it (compose env + mcp_run_new, which must stay in parity)'
No mention of updating deployment docs or an ADR beyond referencing existing ADR 0104 for the opcert decision.
findings.finding: The fix introduces a new deployment config surface (REBAR_ROOT env in compose + mcp_run_new, a new provisioned clone path /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code) but names no doc/ADR/AGENTS.md update capturing the new repo-root provisioning contract and the compose/mcp_run_new parity requirement.
scenarios: A future operator changes compose but not mcp_run_new (or vice versa) and re-introduces the drift because the parity requirement is not documented anywhere durable.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an observable signal (log line or marker file) that distinguishes code-clone converging / converged / failed, so a gate ref-resolution error is diagnosable.
evidence: 'Until it converges the gates fail exactly as they do today — no worse.'
'A failed code clone therefore degrades to today's behaviour — the gates error.'
No stated log/metric for clone-in-progress vs clone-failed; a blobless clone also fetches objects on demand, so a transient remote outage at gate time is a distinct failure mode not addressed.
findings.finding: The backgrounded code clone is a new external failure point (git fetch, plus on-demand blob fetch during gate ops due to --filter=blob:none), but the plan surfaces no metric/log/marker distinguishing 'clone still converging' from 'clone failed' — operators and agents see only the same generic gate ref-resolution error.
findings.location: Fix section 'Ordering' + 'Enforcement is OUT OF SCOPE'
scenarios: An operator investigating a stuck ticket cannot tell whether to wait (converging) or intervene (clone failed) because both present identically.
The blobless clone needs the remote at gate time to fetch missing blobs; if the remote is unreachable then, the gate fails even after a 'successful' clone.
findings.suggested_fix: Have the backgrounded provisioner write a status marker (e.g. mcp-code/.provision_status) and log clone start/success/failure; note whether blob:none on-demand fetches at gate time are acceptable given remote availability.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that plan_review_status can report 'certified' without a verifiable (non-foreign) signature, or add a dependency edge to dire-expectable-terrapin and note that AC3 requires its resolution.
evidence: AC3: 'A PASS from AC1 persists a signed plan-review attestation, so plan_review_status on that ticket reports certified.'
Scope note: 'the environment holds no public key, so verify_signature returns foreign_key ... is NOT in scope here.'
A signature that returns foreign_key on verification may prevent a 'certified' status, creating tension between an in-scope AC and an out-of-scope defect.
findings.finding: AC3 requires plan_review_status to report 'certified' after a PASS, but the scope note states the signing environment holds no public key so verify_signature returns foreign_key (tracked as dire-expectable-terrapin, out of scope). The plan does not establish that 'certified' status is reachable independently of signature verification — if certification consumes the same verify path, AC3 may be unsatisfiable by this ticket alone.
findings.location: AC3 vs 'Scope boundaries — A shared op-cert is acceptable'
scenarios: Fix lands, clone converges, review_plan PASSes and signs, but plan_review_status stays uncertified because the opcert's public key is foreign to the verifying environment.
findings.suggested_fix: Either cite that 'certified' is derived from attestation presence (not signature verification) — quoting the code path — or add a depends_on edge to dire-expectable-terrapin and scope AC3 accordingly.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the convergence-wait or retry protocol for AC1/AC2/DD1 (e.g. verify after the code-clone status marker reports converged, or poll up to N seconds).
evidence: 'Like the tickets clone this is backgrounded ... Until it converges the gates fail exactly as they do today.'
AC1: 'against the deployed MCP server returns a plan-review verdict' — no stated convergence-wait or retry window.
findings.finding: AC1/AC2/DD1 verify against 'the deployed MCP server' but, because the clone is backgrounded, do not state whether verification waits for convergence — an executor could observe the pre-convergence error and be unsure if the fix failed or is merely still cloning.
scenarios: Executor runs AC1 immediately post-deploy before the background clone finishes, sees the ref error, and cannot tell whether the fix is broken.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the ACs: 'evaluated after the code clone has converged (per its status marker), or retried until convergence within the readiness window.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the code clone at /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code keeps origin/main current (periodic/background git fetch, operation-linked refresh, or an explicit statement that provision-time freshness is acceptable and why it differs from the rejected frozen-.git approach).
evidence: Plan rejects shipping .git because it 'pins a main that goes stale the moment the image is built — the gates need a ref that tracks main, not a frozen one.'
'clones the CODE side into /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code — --filter=blob:none --single-branch --branch main' — a one-time clone with no stated fetch/refresh mechanism.

A --single-branch clone's origin/main is only as fresh as its last fetch; the plan defines CREATE but not UPDATE, so the clone's main becomes stale identically to the frozen-image case the plan argues against.
findings.finding: The provisioned blobless clone at /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code is created once at provision time with --single-branch --branch main, but the plan specifies no UPDATE (periodic fetch) or RETIRE/re-clone lifecycle — so origin/main in the clone freezes at provision-time, reintroducing exactly the staleness the plan rejects for the .dockerignore alternative.
scenarios: A container that has run for days resolves attested gates against a main that is many commits behind actual origin/main, silently producing verdicts against a stale base ref.
review_plan/verify_completion return verdicts computed against an outdated main, which may PASS/BLOCK incorrectly relative to current main.
findings.suggested_fix: State the refresh mechanism (e.g. a backgrounded periodic `git -C /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code fetch origin main` or a fetch on gate invocation) or explicitly justify why a provision-time snapshot is acceptable here when it was rejected for the image.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the mcp-code clone keeps origin/main current (periodic/background `git fetch`, operation-linked refresh, or state that per-deploy re-clone is the intended refresh cadence and is acceptable).
evidence: Plan: 'the gates need a ref that tracks main, not a frozen one' (argued against shipping .git)
Plan: clone is '--single-branch --branch main ... blobless clone that fetches objects on demand' — describes lazy blob fetch, NOT ref updates
Absence: no periodic `git fetch`/`git remote update` or operation-linked refresh is specified for the code root, unlike a mechanism that would keep origin/main advancing
Existing tickets clone (mcp-entrypoint.sh:139) is likewise a one-shot `git clone --single-branch`, so parity alone does not add refresh
findings.finding: The plan provisions a durable `--single-branch --branch main --filter=blob:none` clone at /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code but never states how that root is kept current with origin/main after the initial clone; a single-branch clone does not auto-track, so origin/main will freeze at provision time — the same 'frozen main goes stale' failure the plan rejects for the ship-.git alternative.
scenarios: main advances after the container's code clone completes; gates resolve origin/main to a stale commit and review/verify against outdated code without erroring — a silent-staleness drift, harder to detect than today's hard error
findings.suggested_fix: State the refresh contract for the code root — e.g. a background `git -C /var/gerrit/site/mcp-code fetch --filter=blob:none origin main` on the same cadence/trigger as provisioning, or an explicit note that each blue/green deploy re-provisions the clone so main can only be as stale as the current image.
